Table of Contents

Act Fast Because Time Is Critical

The faster you begin working on pet stains and odors, the better chance you have to eliminate them. The moment you notice your pet has left a stain or had an accident, you must get going with the cleaning techniques outlined in this post.

If a pet stain has time to set it, it moves deeper and deeper into your furniture and gets harder to eliminate. It’s better not to work harder than you have to, so act fast and make your odor-removing task easier. Now, there’s no need for you to add this up to your deep cleaning house checklist, as you need to act fast on this matter.

It’s possible to get rid of pet odors and stains after they set in, but the task is harder. Save your energy by staying vigilant and always ready to clean up if your pet has an unfortunate accident.

Which Household Products Work For Pet Stain And Odor Removal On Furniture?

Many household cleaners that you may already have in your pantry or medicine cabinet work for pet stain and odor removal. Some things that could help you with this task include:

  • Vinegar – the acidity kills bacteria that could cause odors.
  • Baking soda – this multi-purpose item absorbs odors like no other.
  • Dish soap – not just for dishes, this is great for getting protein-rich pet stains off of furniture.
  • Salt – if a stain is greasy, sprinkle some regular table salt onto your furniture, let it absorb the grease, and then vacuum it up.

Professional house cleaning servicesin Falls Church, VA might use a more aggressive product. However, it would be best not to use them if you’re going to do the cleaning yourself. These products are all effective on pet stains and odors. The things listed above are the first part of removal after your animal makes a mess in the house.

Specialty products pet stains and odor products, like enzyme cleaners, break down the odor-causing compounds in pet urine and feces. You can do a search for pet stain and odor best enzyme cleaners to find the toughest products on the market.

Don’t Rub Pet Stains, Blot At Them

All too many people are used to rubbing on messes to clean them up. That is one of the worst things you can do, especially on a piece of upholstered furniture. Rubbing actually puts the stain deeper into the fibers, making the stain harder to clean.

Instead, use a clean and super-absorbent rag. First, lay the rag on top of the pet stain, then gently press on the stain to get the liquid to come up. You can blot the stain and get as much of it up as you can this way.

Once you get as much of the stain up as possible, you can apply the items listed above to the area. In the end, you need to blot the product up as well. Then flush it all out with some plain water.

Use A Drying Compound, Then Vacuum

The drying compounds you can use are baking soda or salt, or you may find some other product. These dry items go on and absorb any leftover liquid that could cause odors down the road.

Sprinkle a healthy amount of your drying material onto the stain, and make sure that all of the moisture gets absorbed. Wait at least ten minutes for your drying material to absorb any pet stain and odor that is left on your furniture.

Finally, use the right vacuum attachment to suck up the drying compound that is saturated with the pet stain and odor. Don’t use a carpet attachment, it could break up the absorbed materials and put them back into your furniture. This is one good way to avoid mold from developing. However, if you think you have mold growing on your furniture, it would be best to look for tips on cleaning moldand add them up to your cleaning regimen.

Vinegar Is Perfect For Soaking Pet Stain And Odor

If you got the stain a little late, you might want to apply some vinegar and let it sit for some minutes on your furniture. White vinegar is the usual choice because it is the cheapest kind, but almost any type of vinegar should work.

Dilute the vinegar up to 50 percent if you are worried about damaging your upholstery furniture with the acid. You might want to test the vinegar on an inconspicuous section to make sure it won’t damage your furniture.

Once the vinegar has sat on your furniture for up to an hour, blot it up with a clean absorbent towel. You could then apply some water, then let the section dry, and make sure there are no remaining odors.

Dish Soap Works Wonders On Cat Urine And Other Pet Stains And Odors

Cat urine is rich in protein, and a great way to lift up that protein out of your furniture is with some common dish soap. Mix ten drops of dish soap with one cup of water, then apply it to your pet’s stain and odor.

Blot up the mixture as soon as you can and keep adding more until you can’t see any more stains. Next, you have to let the area dry and see if all of the pet stains and odors are gone.

Preventing Pet Stains And Odors Is The Best Method

Doing an excellent job of cleaning up your pet stain and odor will help to make it less likely that an accident will happen again. If your pet was sick when the accident happened, make sure to take them to a veterinarian and address their concerns.

Training your pet to go to the bathroom in the right place could seem difficult, but with the right techniques, you can do it. Then you won’t ever have to worry about cleaning your furniture from pet stains and odors again.
